original_question: Must homotopic closed geodesics in a manifold of dimension ≥ 3 with no conjugate points be homotopic through closed geodesics?
target_in_paper: Question 7.2.1 in §7.2 (“Parallel postulate questions”) of the final arXiv v3/published version.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It has the right geometric setting (no conjugate points), the right objects (homotopic closed geodesics), the right higher-dimensional restriction (the nearby discussion explains the 2-dimensional case is affirmative, so the open issue is in dimension at least 3), and the right conclusion being asked for (a homotopy through closed geodesics, not just an arbitrary homotopy).
missing_details: Specify that the ambient object is a connected Riemannian manifold (M,g), since both geodesics and the condition ‘no conjugate points’ are metric notions.
Clarify that ‘homotopic’ here means freely homotopic as closed curves/loops, not basepoint-preserving homotopy.
Clarify that ‘homotopic through closed geodesics’ means there is a continuous 1-parameter family of closed geodesics joining the two given ones.
Keep the question exactly at the paper’s scope: do not add compactness, completeness, nonpositive curvature, or other extra hypotheses, because they are not part of the stated question.
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least 3 with no conjugate points. If γ0 and γ1 are closed g-geodesics that are freely homotopic as closed curves in M, must there exist a continuous map H:S^1×[0,1]→M such that H(·,0)=γ0, H(·,1)=γ1, and for every s∈[0,1] the loop H(·,s) is a closed g-geodesic?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft: the paper states in §7.2, Question 7.2.1, the problem of whether homotopic closed geodesics in dimension at least 3 and without conjugate points can be joined by a homotopy through closed geodesics. The surrounding paragraph explains that the answer is positive in dimension 2, and the next remarks isolate the unresolved issue in higher dimensions: although one still gets strong restrictions such as equal length and connectedness inside the fixed-length closed-curve space, the path-connectedness of the closed-geodesic locus is unclear. Section 1 supplies the standing convention that M is a connected manifold and that geodesics are those of the chosen Riemannian metric.
